name: Zipporah
bio:
Zipporah is the daughter of Jethro (also called Reuel), the priest of Midian, and the wife Moses married while shepherding in the Midianite wilderness. After Moses rescued her and her sisters from harassment by other shepherds, Jethro welcomed him and gave him Zipporah in marriage; the couple had two sons, Gershom and Eliezer (Exodus 2:16-22; 18:2-4).

On the journey back to Egypt, Zipporah plays a role in a brief but pivotal and puzzling episode: the LORD met Moses at a lodging place and sought to kill him; Zipporah quickly took a flint and circumcised her son, touching his feet with it and saying, "Surely a bloody husband art thou to me" — an act that saved Moses' life and shows Zipporah's decisiveness in crisis and her regard for the covenant sign of circumcision (Exodus 4:24-26). She was later sent back to her father's house for a time, until Jethro brought her and the two boys to reunite with Moses in the wilderness (Exodus 18).
